arxiv-2010-01454.title: MIME: MIMicking Emotions for Empathetic Response Generation
arxiv-2010-01454.creator: Navonil Majumder, Pengfei Hong, Shanshan Peng, Jiankun Lu, Deepanway Ghosal, Alexander Gelbukh, Rada Mihalcea, Soujanya Poria
arxiv-2010-01454.description: Abstract Current approaches to empathetic response generation view the set of emotions expressed in the input text as a flat structure, where all the emotions are treated uniformly. We argue that empathetic responses often mimic the emotion of the user to a varying degree, depending on its positivity or negativity and content.

arxiv-2106-13439.title: Extensions of the Maximum Bichromatic Separating Rectangle Problem
arxiv-2106-13439.creator: Bogdan Armaselu
arxiv-2106-13439.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Bogdan Armaselu. In this paper, we study two extensions of the maximum bichromatic separating rectangle (MBSR) problem introduced in [ 2 , 4 ] . One of the extensions, introduced in [ 3 ] , is called MBSR with outliers or MBSR-O, and is a more general version of the MBSR problem in which the optimal rectangle is allowed to contain up to k k outliers, where k k is given as part of the input.

arxiv-2109-15049.title: Quantum Identity-Based Encryption from the Learning with Errors Problem
arxiv-2109-15049.creator: Wenhua Gao 1,2,3 , Li Yang 1,2,3 , Daode Zhang, Xia Liu 1,2,3
arxiv-2109-15049.description: Abstract . In order to prevent eavesdropping and tampering, the network security protocols use a handshake with an asymmetric cipher to establish a session-specific shared key with which further communication is encrypted using a symmetric cipher. The commonly used asymmetric algorithms include public key encryption, key exchange and identity-based encryption (IBE).

arxiv-2201-09128.title: Amplitude Ratios and Neural Network Quantum States
arxiv-2201-09128.creator: Vojtěch Havlíček
arxiv-2201-09128.description: Abstract Neural Network Quantum States (NQS) represent quantum wavefunctions by artificial neural networks. Here we study the wavefunction access provided by NQS defined in [Science, 355 , 6325, pp. 602-606 (2017)] and relate it to results from distribution testing. This leads to improved distribution testing algorithms for such NQS.

arxiv-2402-06137.description: Abstract Report Noisy Max and Above Threshold are two classical differentially private (DP) selection mechanisms. Their output is obtained by adding noise to a sequence of low-sensitivity queries and reporting the identity of the query whose (noisy) answer satisfies a certain condition. Pure DP guarantees for these mechanisms are easy to obtain when Laplace noise is added to the queries.

arxiv-2511-11169.title: Refine and Align: Confidence Calibration through Multi-Agent Interaction in VQA
arxiv-2511-11169.creator: Ayush Pandey, Jai Bardhan, Ishita Jain, Ramya S Hebbalaguppe, Rohan Raju Dhanakshirur, Lovekesh Vig
arxiv-2511-11169.description: Abstract In the context of Visual Question Answering (VQA) and Agentic AI, calibration refers to how closely an AI system’s confidence in its answers reflects their actual correctness. This aspect becomes especially important when such systems operate autonomously and must make decisions under visual uncertainty.

arxiv-2512-05996.title: FishDetector-R1: Unified MLLM-Based Framework with Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Weakly Supervised Fish Detection, Segmentation, and Counting
arxiv-2512-05996.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by . Analyzing underwater fish imagery is critical for ecological monitoring but remains difficult due to visual degradation and costly annotations. We introduce FishDetector-R1 , a unified MLLM-based framework for fish detection, segmentation, and counting under weak supervision . On the DeepFish dataset, our framework achieves substantial gains over baselines, improving AP by 20% and mIoU by 10%, while reducing MAE by 30% and GAME by 35%.

uslaw-usc-t21-s154a.title: 21 U.S.C. § 154a — Special licenses for special circumstances; expedited procedure; conditions; exemptions; criteria
uslaw-usc-t21-s154a.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t21-s154a.description: United States Code, Title 21 (Food And Drugs); Chapter 5 (Viruses, Serums, Toxins, Antitoxins, And Analogous Products). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. In order to meet an emergency condition, limited market or local situation, or other special circumstance (including production solely for intrastate use under a State-operated program), the Secretary may issue a special license under an expedited procedure on such conditions.
